paraphrased_evidence: Kvothe says the University now hosts over a thousand students, and admissions begins each term with a lottery followed by interviews over eleven days; long lines snake through the courtyard while students mill about after drawing tiles.
what_this_proves: The University is large enough that admissions is a major logistical event requiring outdoor queueing and crowd management.
contradictions_or_open_questions: Exact student count beyond “over a thousand” not given.

building_or_room_name: Wide cobblestone courtyard / older “House of the Wind”
paraphrased_evidence: Kvothe is whipped in a wide cobblestone courtyard that “used to be called the Quoyan Hayel,” meaning House of the Wind; hundreds of students fill it to overflowing, with others watching from windows, doorways, and rooftops.
what_this_proves: This is a large central courtyard designed or reused for public disciplinary events and surrounded by occupied buildings with accessible windows, doors, and roofs.
contradictions_or_open_questions: Open question whether this is the same place later/elsewhere called Pennant Square or Questioning Hall in other passages.

paraphrased_evidence: Students wait in a hallway outside Elodin’s class, then enter a huge empty lecture hall and walk down stairs to the front row; a large slate stands at the front.
what_this_proves: The room is tiered, entered from above or mid-level, and built like a descending lecture theatre rather than a flat classroom.
contradictions_or_open_questions: Building not named in this passage.

paraphrased_evidence: Kvothe says the Archives is not merely a warehouse but “like a city unto itself,” with roads, winding lanes, alleys, and shortcuts.
what_this_proves: The Archives has a large, navigable internal layout with multiple route types and nontrivial wayfinding.
contradictions_or_open_questions: Metaphorical language, but tied directly to circulation and therefore useful spatial evidence.

paraphrased_evidence: The Scriptorium contains rows of desks where scrivs translate texts and copy fading books into new volumes.
what_this_proves: The Archives includes a dedicated large workroom arranged for many seated workers.
contradictions_or_open_questions: No floor or adjacency given.

paraphrased_evidence: The Sorting Hall “buzzed with activity” as scrivs sorted and reshelved books.
what_this_proves: There is a distinct internal processing area for returned / displaced books, separate from simple storage.
contradictions_or_open_questions: Exact size and placement not stated.

paraphrased_evidence: The Buggery is where new books are decontaminated before being added to the collection because many creatures infest books.
what_this_proves: The Archives has a quarantine / processing zone between acquisition and shelving.
contradictions_or_open_questions: No layout details beyond function.

paraphrased_evidence: Cataloger’s Mew is listed among busy scriv spaces, “full of quiet, industrious scrivs.”
what_this_proves: The Archives contains a specialised cataloguing area rather than a single undifferentiated work floor.
contradictions_or_open_questions: Exact physical form unknown despite the name “Mew.”

paraphrased_evidence: The Bindery is one of several named internal Archives work areas busy with scrivs.
what_this_proves: Book repair / binding is housed within the Archives complex itself.
contradictions_or_open_questions: No explicit architectural detail beyond being a distinct named zone.

paraphrased_evidence: “Bolts” is named as one of the active internal Archives work areas.
what_this_proves: Confirms another distinct sub-area within the Archives.
contradictions_or_open_questions: Function not explained here.

paraphrased_evidence: “Palimpsest” is named alongside other busy Archives work areas.
what_this_proves: Confirms another distinct named sub-area inside the Archives.
contradictions_or_open_questions: Function not explained here.

paraphrased_evidence: The acquisitions office is described as tiny and perpetually dark. One whole wall is covered by a huge lacquered map with cities and roads in great detail and marked with red grease-pencil notes showing rumours of desirable books and the last known positions of acquisition teams.
what_this_proves: The Archives has a specialised, probably restricted office for collection strategy, and it houses a major wall map used operationally.
contradictions_or_open_questions: No direct statement of who can enter freely.

paraphrased_evidence: Kvothe says Tomes is like a great public garden, and any student is free to come and read the books shelved there.
what_this_proves: Tomes is the publicly accessible reading collection of the Archives, distinct from more restricted areas.
contradictions_or_open_questions: Whether “any student” means literally all students or only students in good standing is not unpacked here.

paraphrased_evidence: Lorren says Kvothe is reckless and had intended to keep him out of the Archives for “a year and a day.” Elodin gets that reduced to “Tomes only.” Lorren says his concern is “for the Archives itself.”
what_this_proves: Access within the Archives is tiered, and sanctions can restrict a student to Tomes while excluding deeper access.
contradictions_or_open_questions: The passage does not restate exactly what deeper privileges were being withheld, though Stacks is the likely implication.

paraphrased_evidence: Elodin steals the key to the roof of the Archives; once trapped there, he and Kvothe spend the night on the bare stone rooftop in a storm. The next morning Lorren has several strong scrivs batter down the door leading to the roof because no second key seems available. Help is called down to the courtyard below.
what_this_proves: The Archives has a roof accessed by a locked interior door, the roof surface is stone and exposed, and it overlooks a courtyard where people below can hear voices from above.
contradictions_or_open_questions: Exact roof entry point inside the building is not specified.

paraphrased_evidence: Kvothe goes to Ledgers and Lists to sign up for classes, including Medica, Fishery, Sympathy, and Elodin’s class.
what_this_proves: The University has a distinct administrative registration office or records room for course enrolment.
contradictions_or_open_questions: No architectural description beyond function.

paraphrased_evidence: On returning to work, Kvothe notices the light is unusual because sunlight is slanting through the low windows on the eastern wall. The huge room feels hollow and lifeless with only a handful of students in it early in the morning.
what_this_proves: The workshop is very large, has exterior windows on at least its eastern wall, and those windows are relatively low-set.
contradictions_or_open_questions: “Low” is clear; exact window height and count are not.

paraphrased_evidence: Kilvin’s office opens off the workshop. It has a small forge or glasswork in the corner, is hot from the stoked fire, and Kvothe swings the heavy door closed behind him.
what_this_proves: Kilvin’s office is an enclosed room inside the Fishery with a substantial door and its own working hot apparatus.
contradictions_or_open_questions: Whether the apparatus is permanently installed or temporarily set up is not fully explicit, though it reads as fixed workspace.

paraphrased_evidence: Basil says the girl looking for Kvothe has been lingering in the courtyard, and he jerks his head toward the southern exit of the Fishery.
what_this_proves: The Fishery has at least one south-facing exit that opens toward or gives onto a courtyard.
contradictions_or_open_questions: The courtyard is not otherwise identified.

paraphrased_evidence: Kvothe climbs onto Mains and moves through a “familiar maze of chimneys and mismatched slate and clay and tin.”
what_this_proves: Mains has a complex roofline with multiple chimney stacks and mixed roofing materials, matching its accreted construction.
contradictions_or_open_questions: No exact path system given beyond rooftop navigability.

paraphrased_evidence: Auri leads Kvothe across the roof to the apple tree they can use to climb down into the courtyard.
what_this_proves: At least one courtyard is directly adjacent to Mains or its roof edge, and the tree provides an informal vertical route between roof and ground.
contradictions_or_open_questions: Not clear whether this courtyard is internal to Mains or merely beside it.

paraphrased_evidence: Kvothe says Auri shows him the “vast and varied corners” of the Underthing over many nights.
what_this_proves: The Underthing is extensive, multi-zone, and too large to absorb in a single short visit.
related_locations: DOWNINGS, VAULTS, WOODS, DELVING, CRICKLET, TENNERS, CANDLEBEAR, BELOWS
contradictions_or_open_questions: General statement rather than a precise map.

paraphrased_evidence: The Woods is a set of crumbling halls and rooms whose ceilings are propped up with thick wooden support beams.
what_this_proves: Some Underthing zones are failing structurally and require visible support.
contradictions_or_open_questions: None.

paraphrased_evidence: Cricklet is a long low room with a tiny trickle of fresh water running down one wall, attracting crickets.
what_this_proves: At least part of the Underthing is water-fed, habitable to insects, and low-ceilinged.
contradictions_or_open_questions: None.

paraphrased_evidence: Vaults is a narrow hallway with three deep cracks across the floor.
what_this_proves: The Underthing includes narrow corridor-like sections with damaged flooring that affects movement.
contradictions_or_open_questions: None.

paraphrased_evidence: Auri takes Kvothe to Belows, a maze of intersecting tunnels at least a hundred feet below ground, filled with a steady rushing wind that smells of dust and leather.
what_this_proves: The Underthing extends very deep and includes ventilated tunnel systems with strong airflow, suggesting major hidden connections or shafts.
contradictions_or_open_questions: The exact meaning and spelling of the name remains uncertain in the passage itself.

paraphrased_evidence: After returning, Kvothe says he made his way back across the river before later climbing onto Mains that night.
what_this_proves: The familiar University/Imre separation by river remains active and relevant in WMF travel logic.
contradictions_or_open_questions: The bridge is not restated in this passage, only the river crossing.

paraphrased_evidence: Imre’s streets are busier at night than by day, with music spilling from inns and theatres and crowds moving among restaurants and exhibition halls. Kvothe later walks back to the University from there.
what_this_proves: Imre remains a dense evening social district contrasted with the University side; pedestrian movement between the two is routine.
contradictions_or_open_questions: Atmospheric but still useful for settlement function; does not add precise layout.

paraphrased_evidence: Approaching along an exterior ledge/roofline, Kvothe finds one stained-glass window that does not open and another wide double window with a simple latch, added drop bar, and a sash stuck shut; there is about a fifteen-foot drop outside.
what_this_proves: At least one high-status residence in Imre has layered physical security at the window and is accessible only by risky roofline movement from outside.
contradictions_or_open_questions: This is Imre evidence, not University proper.

paraphrased_evidence: Through the window Kvothe sees dim lamps and a canopy bed as big as his room at Anker’s.
what_this_proves: Ambrose’s lodging is large and luxurious, with oversized furnishings relative to ordinary student rooms.
contradictions_or_open_questions: Exact building not named in this passage.
